title: /find-callers with Grep scoped to TypeScript
situation: A payments platform's developer productivity team is adding a /find-callers command that should locate every reference to a renamed helper function, limit the search to TypeScript source files, and return enough context for a developer to jump directly to each match.
question: Which Claude Code built-in tool configuration should the command use?

options.A: Use Glob with pattern **/<helper-name>.ts, sort the returned paths, and treat matching file names as caller locations.
options.B: Use Glob with pattern **/*.ts, then Read each file and load all contents into the conversation for scanning.
options.C: Use Bash to run grep -r <helper-name> --include=*.ts, then parse stdout as caller locations.
options.D: Use Grep with the helper name as pattern, scope with glob **/*.ts, and set output_mode: content for matching lines.

why: Grep is the Claude Code built-in tool intended for searching file contents such as function names, error messages, and import statements. References to a renamed helper function are content inside source files, so the search should be expressed as a Grep pattern rather than a file-name lookup. Glob is the right tool when the goal is to find files by path or file-name pattern, for example **/*.test.ts. For developer navigation, Grep with output_mode: content returns matching lines with file and line number, and the tool can scope content searches with a glob filter such as **/*.ts. Avoid confusing the built-in Grep tool with invoking the shell command grep through Bash; the built-in tool has documented behavior and configuration surfaces in Claude Code, while shell commands are handled separately through Bash permissions. (Docs: Claude Code tools reference, permissions.)
expected_outcome: The command returns path:line locations for formatDate inside .ts files only, using the built-in Grep tool with a glob filter and output_mode content.

rubric.criterion: TypeScript callers come back as path:line
JavaScript callers are excluded by the glob
